challenges.name: reading-input-quiz
challenges.title: Predict what std::cin reads
challenges.description: Follow the read position through the input buffer: what does each read consume, what does it leave behind, and when does the loop really stop?

questions.explanation: Round 1: >> reads RP-01 and stops at the space, getline reads the rest of the line, " An" WITH its leading space, and eats the newline. Round 2 does the same for RP-02 and " Bình". Now every character has been read, but eof() is still false: getline stopped at the newline and never tried to read past it. So the loop runs a third time. This time >> finds the end of input, sets eofbit and failbit, and leaves id unchanged; getline on a failed stream does nothing, so name is unchanged too. records is 3, id is RP-02, name is " Bình". "2 ..." would be right only for while (std::cin >> id && std::getline(std::cin, name)). "[Bình]" without the space forgets that getline keeps the space after the id (only >> std::ws would remove it). "3 [] []" assumes a failed read clears the strings - it does not, the variables keep their last values.

questions.question: Each line of a score file looks like "RP-01 8.5 Trần Văn An" and the file ends with a newline. Which loops call handle(line) exactly once per line, with the whole line, and stop after the last one? (Select all that apply.) Assume std::string line; is declared before each loop where needed.
questions.explanation: A loop is correct when the read itself is the loop condition: the body runs only after a read that succeeded. while (std::getline(std::cin, line)) and the for form (which also keeps line local to the loop) do that - in a real run on two lines they called handle twice. while (!std::cin.eof()) and while (std::cin) test the stream BEFORE the read: after the last line both are still true, getline then fails at the end of input and leaves line empty, and handle is called a third time with "". while (std::cin >> line) checks its read, but >> reads one word, not one line: on the two-line file it called handle 9 times, with RP-01, 8.5, Trần, Văn, An and so on.

challenges.name: fix-score-file-reader
challenges.title: Make the score-file reader check every line
challenges.description: The ported score-file reader prints a course report for the exam office: one line per student and the average. On every file it prints an empty record with score 0.0 right after the course code and another one at the end, which drags the average down. A score typed as "8,5" is printed as 8.0 with ",5" glued to the name, and a score field like "abc" becomes 0. Fix process_score_file so that it reads the file line by line, prints every good record, reports every bad line with its line number without stopping, and computes the average from the good records only. The header comment in the starter gives the exact rules and output format.

tests.name: Two good records with spaces in the names
tests.input:
CS101
RP-2024-0137 8.5 Nguyễn Thị Phương Thảo
RP-2024-0138 7 Trần Văn An
tests.expected:
CS101
RP-2024-0137 | Nguyễn Thị Phương Thảo | 8.5
RP-2024-0138 | Trần Văn An | 7.0
records: 2, bad: 0, average: 7.75
